# Lab 01 — The governance gap

**PART I — Why governed agentic systems are needed**  
*Ch. 2 — The Governance Gap*

`beginner` · about 15 minutes

```bash
nornyx-lab run 01      # run it
nornyx-lab check 01    # prove you got it
```

Four files that each look reasonable, disagree with each other, and are bound to
nothing. Then one file that generates them.

## By the end of this lab you will be able to

- Inventory the informal controls a team accumulates around an agent
- Explain why they form a distributed control system with no protocol
- Name and identify the four kinds of drift
- Generate coordinated artifacts from one contract instead of maintaining four

## What the lab does, in order

1. Part 1 — the inventory
2. Part 2 — the agent obeys the file that was written for it
3. Part 3 — the four kinds of drift
4. Part 4 — one source, generated artifacts

## What `check` proves

Each item is one proposition, written so a machine can settle it.
That is the habit the whole book teaches: a governance claim you
cannot express as a test is not yet a claim.

- the scattered controls actually contradict
- an agent following agents md merges without tests
- the contract is valid
- generation produces the scattered artifacts from one source
- generation is byte deterministic
- generated artifacts are derived not authoritative

## Concepts introduced

- `governance debt`
- `control drift`
- `policy drift`
- `configuration drift`
- `framework-adapter drift`
- `single source of truth`
